title: Interview Calibration and Hiring Scorecard Guidelines
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose: Provide a single, operationalized set of rules and artifacts for interview panels, scorecards, and cross-functional calibration to improve hiring quality, reduce bias, and standardize decision-making across Redwood Inference. This doc aligns recruiters, hiring managers, interviewers, and people-ops on process, responsibilities, and measurable SLAs.

Scope: Applies to all full-time and long-term contract hires globally unless a role is marked as ‘legal/security restricted’ (see Compliance section). Does not replace role-specific technical evaluation guides maintained by each engineering sub-team; instead it defines the wrapper process for consistent evaluation and calibration.

Key outcomes
- Consistent scorecards used for every candidate at on-site / final-stage interviews
- Structured calibration meetings with artifacts stored in the ATS for auditability
- Candidate experience SLAs: responses and next steps timelines
- Centralized metrics to monitor panel effectiveness and hiring bias indicators

Roles & responsibilities
- Hiring Manager: owns the job rubric, defines top-3 success outcomes for the role, selects panel, makes the final hiring recommendation (in partnership with people-ops).
- Recruiter: schedules interviews, ensures scorecards are completed by panel within 48 hours, prepares calibration packet, executes offer logistics.
- Interviewers/Panelists: evaluate using the scorecard, document behavioral evidence, and attend calibration.
- People Ops (Hiring Partner): facilitates final calibration, validates compensation band, ensures compliance with EEO and background-check policies.
- Legal/Privacy: reviews privileged roles and approves any deviations to standard process.

Interview panel composition guidelines
- Minimum: 3 interviewers for final-stage loop (one peer, one cross-functional stakeholder, hiring manager).
- Balanced perspectives: include at least one interviewer outside the immediate team for broad context.
- Diversity: strive for demographic and seniority diversity on panels where possible; document constraints when not feasible.
- Conflict-of-interest rule: anyone with a personal relationship (family or close friend) to the candidate must recuse.

Standard scorecard template (required fields)
- Overall recommendation (Hire / No Hire / Hire with reservations) — single choice.
- Competency buckets (each scored 1–5 with behavioral evidence):
  - Role-specific technical skills (e.g., model-serving, infra, SDK design)
  - Problem solving and system design
  - Collaboration and communication
  - Delivery and ownership
  - Cultural add / alignment with Redwood values
- Candidate risks & open questions (free text)
- Compensation expectation (if disclosed) and interview notes about negotiation constraints
- Interviewer confidence level (low / medium / high)

Scoring rubric and thresholds
- 1 = Does not meet the bar; 2 = Below expectations; 3 = Meets expectations (baseline); 4 = Above expectations; 5 = Exceptional.
- Passing rule for final-stage: median score >= 3 and no competency bucket with median <= 2.
- Clear hire signal: >=3 interviewers with score >=4 and at least two interviewers with high confidence.
- No-hire veto: any documented legal/security concern, or unanimous scores <=2.

Calibration workflow (step-by-step)
1) Recruiter compiles packet: resume, anonymized scorecards (redact demographic PII), coding/system design artifacts, and recommended compensation band. Packet must be uploaded to the ATS 24 hours before calibration.
2) Panel attends a scheduled 45–60 minute calibration meeting within 72 hours of final interview. If panelists disagree strongly (>2 pt variance on the same competency), a deeper technical follow-up may be scheduled.
3) Calibration meeting agenda: 10m candidate recap (recruiter), 20–30m scorecard review and discussion, 10m risk assessment and reference checks plan, 10m decision and next steps.
4) Final decision recorded in the ATS immediately after meeting with all scorecards attached and a 2–3 sentence hiring rationale from the hiring manager.

Decision governance & escalation
- Hiring Manager has the primary recommendation authority but cannot extend an offer until people-ops confirms compensation and compliance checks.
- In cases of tied or close decisions, the hiring manager must escalate to the Business Unit Hiring Committee (BUHC) within 48 hours. The BUHC consists of a senior engineering leader, a senior product leader, and a people-ops representative.
- For executive-level and privileged roles, a second-stage interview with Security and Legal is mandatory before any offer.

Candidate experience SLAs (operational targets)
- Acknowledgement of application: within 48 hours of application receipt.
- Recruiter intro call scheduled: within 5 business days of application passing screen.
- Feedback after final interview (offer or rejection): within 72 hours of calibration decision.
- Offer expiry standard: 7 business days (exceptions handled by hiring partner).

Bias mitigation & structured interviewing rules
- Use the standard scorecard; free-text-only evaluations are not accepted for final-stage decisions.
- Interviewers must record behavioral evidence for any score <=2 or >=4 to justify extremes.
- Avoid hypothetical questions tied to demographic assumptions. Use scenario-based prompts aligned to the rubric.
- Where possible, anonymize early-stage work sample reviews for initial technical screening.

Data, metrics, and reporting
- Tracked KPIs (reported weekly to People Ops and hiring managers): time-to-offer median, offer acceptance rate, panel no-show rate, percent of hires passing probation, diversity funnel metrics per stage.
- Quality KPIs (monthly): new-hire retention @90 days, hiring manager satisfaction score (post-hire survey), calibration variance (average stdev per competency across panels).
- Thresholds to trigger a hiring process review: time-to-offer > 28 days (median) sustained for 2 consecutive months, offer acceptance rate < 65% in a quarter, calibration variance > 1.0 average.

Onboarding handoff checklist (to be completed before offer is accepted if possible)
- Job description final copy and first-90-day success plan attached to candidate record.
- Tools and access list drafted (engineering onboarding owner to attach required infra access).
- Manager onboarding tasks scheduled (first-week 1:1s, codebase walkthrough, security onboarding).
- HR forms queued and background check initiation ready to trigger upon offer acceptance.

Compensation & offer timing guidance
- Recruiters propose initial offer within band and include a short justification memo referencing market data or internal comp-equivalents.
- People Ops must approve final compensation within 48 hours of calibration decision before recruiter extends an offer.
- For high-priority roles identified by the hiring manager and recruiter, use fast-track approval: defined as roles with <7 day time-to-fill target; fast-track requires BUHC pre-approval of band.

Legal, background checks, and data privacy
- Standard background checks: employment verification and criminal background where permitted by local law. Certain regulated roles require additional checks (list maintained by Legal).
- Candidate PII handling: only recruiter, hiring manager, and people-ops should retain full PII. Publicly stored artifacts (e.g., scorecards) must have PII redacted.
- International hires: ensure visa and tax obligations are reviewed with Finance and Legal before offers. For offshore contractors, include contractor compliance checklist.

Training & interviewer enablement
- Mandatory annual interviewer training covering: structured interviewing, unconscious bias, scorecard use, and Redwood’s values.
- New interviewers must shadow two loops before conducting independent final-stage interviews.
- Interviewer performance tracked and remediated if average variance from panel > 1.2 or repeated low-quality feedback (as measured by hiring manager survey).

Exceptions and deviations
- Any deviation from the required 3-interviewer minimum, scorecard use, or calibration timeline must be documented with rationale and approved by People Ops.

  - Problem solving: "Tell me about a time you diagnosed a production performance regression and the steps you took to isolate and remediate it."
  - Collaboration: "Describe a cross-team disagreement you influenced to a successful outcome."
  - Delivery: "Give an example of a time you had to de-scope features to meet a delivery deadline — what trade-offs did you make?"
